As stated in the medical certificate.
No more than 4 weeks before the expected date.

Maternity leave after the Article 151 amendment

Since 19 February 2025, maternity leave in the private sector has been 12 weeks on full pay, with no minimum service. The worker may arrange it as she wishes, on two conditions: it may not start more than 4 weeks before the expected date of birth, and 6 weeks of it must fall after the birth.

Leave around childbirth in Saudi Arabia

LeaveLengthPay
Maternity leave12 weeks, up to 4 before the birth and at least 6 afterFull pay
Optional extension1 monthUnpaid
Sick or disabled baby1 month, extendable by 1 monthFull pay, then unpaid
Paternity leave3 days within 7 days of the birthFull pay

Example: expected date 1 June 2026, leave from 4 May 2026 (four weeks before). The 84 days end on 26 July 2026, and you are back at work on 27 July — provided the baby arrives on time.

Pay continues in full throughout the leave: on an actual wage of SAR 9,000 that is 84 days × 300 = SAR 25,200, with no deduction. With the optional unpaid month, the return date in the example moves to 27 August 2026 and that month is unpaid.

Other leave for working parents

LeaveLengthBasis
Marriage5 days on full payArticle 113
Death of a spouse, parent or child5 days on full payArticle 113
Death of a brother or sister3 days on full pay (new in 2025)Article 113
Iddah of a Muslim widow4 months and 10 days on full pay, extended unpaid until birth if pregnantArticle 160
Non-Muslim widow15 days on full payArticle 160
Nursing breaksBreaks totalling no more than an hour a day, without a pay cutArticle 154

The ministry's awareness guide says the nursing hour lasts 24 months, while the article itself sets no period. Dates for every type of leave are in the Saudi special leave calculator. A worker who resigns within three months of giving birth keeps her full end-of-service award (Article 87); see the end-of-service calculator.

Frequently asked questions

How long is maternity leave in Saudi Arabia after the 2025 amendments?

12 weeks (84 days) on full pay, up from 10 weeks. The change has been in force since 19 February 2025 under Royal Decree M/44.

Is there a minimum service requirement for maternity pay?

No. Article 152, which linked maternity pay to length of service, was repealed, so an employee is entitled to all 12 weeks on full pay whatever her length of service.

When can maternity leave start?

The employee decides how to spread the weeks, provided the leave starts no more than 4 weeks before the expected delivery date and 6 weeks are taken after the birth. The expected date is set by a certified medical certificate.

What if the baby arrives late?

If the birth is late so that less than 6 weeks of leave remain after it, the shortfall is granted unpaid to complete the 6 compulsory weeks.

Can maternity leave be extended?

Yes. The employee may always extend the leave by one unpaid month. If the baby is sick or has a disability and needs constant care, she gets one month on full pay after maternity leave ends, extendable by one unpaid month.

How much paternity leave is there?

3 days on full pay, taken within 7 days of the birth, under Article 113 as amended in 2025.

Can I be dismissed during pregnancy or leave?

No. The employer may not dismiss or warn of dismissal during pregnancy or maternity leave, including illness arising from pregnancy or delivery for up to 180 days a year (Article 155).
